Here’s how to do it in Google Calendar on desktop while keeping the Zoom link and attendees:

1) Check if it’s recurring (important)
- In Google Calendar (web), click once on the “Teacher Meeting” on Friday 12/12/2025.
- If you see something like “This is a recurring event,” you’ll be asked “This event” vs “The entire series” when editing.
  - Choose **“This event”** so you only move that one instance to Saturday.

2) Quick way: drag-and-drop to Saturday
- In **Week** view (top-right: click “Week”):
  - Locate **Friday 12/12/2025 at 3:00–4:00 pm**.
  - Click and **drag the event straight over to Saturday 12/13/2025** onto the **3:00–4:00 pm** slot.
- When you drop it, Google Calendar keeps:
  - The **title** (“Teacher Meeting”)
  - The **Zoom link** (under the video conferencing section)
  - All **attendees**

3) Or use the edit dialog (more precise)
- Click the “Teacher Meeting” on Friday, then click the **pencil icon (Edit)**.
- In the event edit screen:
  - Change the **date** from **Dec 12, 2025** to **Dec 13, 2025**.
  - Make sure the **time** is still **3:00–4:00 pm** and the **time zone** says **Pacific Time**.
- Do **not** change:
  - The “Guests” section (attendees list)
  - The “Google Meet / Zoom” or conferencing section
- Click **Save**.
- If prompted: **“Send update to guests?”**
  - Choose **“Send”** if you want them notified of the date change.
  - Choose **“Don’t send”** if you’ve already told them another way and don’t need an email.

4) Double-check after saving
- Click the event on **Saturday 12/13/2025**:
  - Confirm the **time** is 3:00–4:00 pm.
  - Confirm the **Zoom link** is still there.
  - Open the **Guests** section and make sure everyone is still listed.
